title: A Comprehensive Information-Decomposition Analysis of Large Vision-Language Models
claim: A model-agnostic decomposition pipeline yields a multi-dimensional profile of many models, tasks, layers, and training stages.
layout: 2 stacked sections; top pipeline left-to-right, bottom three columns; dashed dividers
description: The figure has two horizontal sections. The top section shows the proposed PID estimation framework. An image of a truck and a text question pass through a ViT projector and an embedding layer into a Language Model block. Three outputs follow: the multimodal prediction, the vision-only prediction and the language-only prediction. Each is shown with answer probabilities for options A to D. These feed a purple BATCH box, which outputs a bar chart of R, U1, U2 and S: redundancy, vision uniqueness, language uniqueness and synergy. The bottom section lays out three analysis dimensions in columns. (a) lists the 11 model families, 26 models and 4 datasets. (b) stacks Layer 1 through Layer 36, with a bar chart of R, U1, U2 and S beside each layer via a logit lens. (c) shows a two-stage training diagram above a line plot of synergy and language uniqueness. Colors are orange, blue, yellow, red and green.
caption: Overview of this research. The first part is the framework of PID estimation for LVLMs. Given an image-text pair, we extract image and text embeddings as two features, run a standard multimodal forward pass and collect two unimodal predictions by masking the other modality. PID values are estimated with BATCH estimator. The second part reveals three analysis dimensions: (1) cross-model and cross-task comparison, (2) layer-wise information dynamics, and (3) learning dynamics over training. To our knowledge, this is the first comprehensive LVLM analysis through the lens of information decomposition.
abstract: Large vision-language models (LVLMs) achieve impressive performance, yet their internal decision-making processes remain opaque, making it difficult to determine if the success stems from true multimodal fusion or from reliance on unimodal priors. To address this attribution gap, we introduce a novel framework using partial information decomposition (PID) to quantitatively measure the "information spectrum" of LVLMs -- decomposing a model's decision-relevant information into redundant, unique, and synergistic components. By adapting a scalable estimator to modern LVLM outputs, our model-agnostic pipeline profiles 26 LVLMs on four datasets across three dimensions -- breadth (cross-model & cross-task), depth (layer-wise information dynamics), and time (learning dynamics across training). Our analysis reveals two key results: (i) two task regimes (synergy-driven vs. knowledge-driven) and (ii) two stable, contrasting family-level strategies (fusion-centric vs. language-centric). We also uncover a consistent three-phase pattern in layer-wise processing and identify visual instruction tuning as the key stage where fusion is learned. Together, these contributions provide a quantitative lens beyond accuracy-only evaluation and offer insights for analyzing and designing the next generation of LVLMs. Code and data are available at https://github.com/RiiShin/pid-lvlm-analysis .
